the-pianist-2002.gazette: Władysław Szpilman published his account of surviving the Warsaw ghetto in 1946; it went out of print under communist rule and returned to shelves half a century later. The Wehrmacht captain who kept him alive in the ruins, Wilm Hosenfeld, died in Soviet captivity, and Yad Vashem named him Righteous Among the Nations decades afterward. Polanski, who slipped out of the Kraków ghetto as a boy, filmed the adaptation on Polish and German locations.

elephant-2003.gazette: The cast were Portland teenagers with no acting training, most of them keeping their own first names on screen. Van Sant took over a high school that had already closed and let Harris Savides's camera follow them down corridors in takes that last as long as the walk. It took the Palme d'Or in 2003.

timbuktu-2014.gazette: Armed groups held northern Mali through 2012, banning music and running courts of their own. In Aguelhok that July, a couple was stoned to death for living together unmarried, and video of it circulated. Sissako filmed in Mauritania, across the border from the town in the title.
timbuktu-2014.prism: The film had to be shot next door to its own subject, because the town it names was too dangerous to enter. That distance sits inside every wide shot of the desert.

embrace-of-the-serpent-2015.gazette: Two sets of journals frame the film: Theodor Koch-Grünberg's, from a German ethnographer's Amazon expeditions before the First World War, and Richard Evans Schultes's, from an American botanist on the same rivers decades later. Between the two lies the Putumayo rubber boom, where the stations worked Indigenous labour to the point of extermination. Guerra shot in black and white in the Colombian Amazon, with Indigenous actors speaking their own languages.

roma-2018.gazette: On 10 June 1971 a state-trained paramilitary group, Los Halcones, attacked a student march in Mexico City, and the government denied its hand in it for years. Cuarón placed that afternoon inside a domestic story taken from his own childhood, rebuilding the Colonia Roma street he grew up on. The killing reaches the film through a shop window, mid-errand.

1917-2019.gazette: The trenches were dug to period specification in English fields and left to weather before shooting began. Écoust was built as a night set and lit toward Otto Dix's etchings of the Western Front, made by a man who had fought in it. Mendes and Deakins then hid every cut.
1917-2019.prism: Building the war to a checkable standard and then concealing every cut pull against each other — one invites verification, the other refuses it. The seamlessness is the least authentic thing in the film and the thing everyone remembers.

by-the-grace-of-god-2019.gazette: The film uses the real names: Bernard Preynat, the Lyon priest accused of abusing scouts across decades, and Cardinal Philippe Barbarin, accused of leaving him in ministry. Survivors had already organised in public and pushed the case into the courts before Ozon started writing. Preynat's lawyers asked a French court to block the release; the film opened on time in February 2019.

for-sama-2019.gazette: Waad al-Kateab shot in east Aleppo over five years, first as a student in the protests, then as a mother inside the hospital her husband ran. Al-Quds hospital was hit from the air in 2016 and the filming did not stop. When the last convoys left the city that December, the footage went with them.

la-llorona-2019.gazette: A Guatemalan court convicted Efraín Ríos Montt of genocide against the Ixil Maya in May 2013, after weeks of survivor testimony; the Constitutional Court annulled the verdict ten days later. Bustamante rebuilt that courtroom, put a fictional general in the dock, then sealed him inside his own house while crowds held the street outside. The haunting starts where the sentence stopped.
la-llorona-2019.prism: Guatemala got its conviction and lost it inside two weeks, so the film delivers the sentence the court withdrew. The supernatural turns up precisely where the legal system stopped.

the-two-popes-2019.gazette: Benedict XVI resigned the papacy in 2013, the first pope to do so in about six hundred years. The flashbacks go to Argentina in the 1970s, where Jorge Bergoglio led the Jesuits during the junta's disappearances and two priests under his authority were seized and held. The conversations between the two men are invented; the resignation and the detentions are not.

great-freedom-2021.gazette: Paragraph 175 entered German law in 1871 and was widened under the Nazis in 1935. West Germany kept the Nazi wording until 1969, and men freed from the camps were transferred into prisons to finish their terms. The film keeps time by its years — 1945, 1957, 1968 — all of them inside the same cell block.

nitram-2021.gazette: On 28 April 1996 a gunman killed thirty-five people at Port Arthur, Tasmania; twelve days later the states agreed on the National Firearms Agreement. Kurzel's film stops short of that morning and works from the documented family life, the clinical history, and how easily the guns were bought. The name is never said aloud.
nitram-2021.prism: Withholding the name is genuine restraint and also a favourable trade — the film draws on the notoriety of the case without paying for using it. Most of the audience has supplied the name themselves within a scene or two.

prayers-for-the-stolen-2021.gazette: Tatiana Huezo came out of documentary and assembled the film from interviews in the mountains of Guerrero, where the poppy fields are run by cartels and girls disappear. The children on screen were cast locally and mostly untrained, and the hiding pits dug into the dirt come from what survivors described. Nothing in the frame flags itself as reconstruction.

quo-vadis-aida-2021.gazette: Srebrenica was a United Nations safe area, held by a lightly armed Dutch battalion, when the Bosnian Serb army walked in during July 1995 and killed more than eight thousand Bosniak men and boys. International tribunals have called it genocide; Dutch courts have found their own state partly liable. Žbanić watches from inside the base, through the translator who has to say the assurances out loud.

goodbye-dragon-inn-2003.gazette: Tsai filmed inside Taipei's Fu-Ho Grand during the theatre's last stretch of business, using the building as he found it. What runs on the screen inside the screen is King Hu's Dragon Inn from 1967, watched by two of its original actors, now decades older, sitting in the near-empty stalls. The Fu-Ho shut its doors soon after the shoot.
goodbye-dragon-inn-2003.prism: The theatre is subject and set at once, so the film can't be remade — the room is gone. A closing date did as much of the work here as any script.
